description: Decompose the 1074-line SystemUpdateService.cs monolith into per-type files, consolidate duplicated state-transition templates into shared helpers, and fix the command/query separation violation so the status query becomes a pure read while job advancement moves to an explicit command path.

tasks.title: Split SystemUpdateService into one type-group per file
tasks.description: Move each cohesive collaborator type out of SystemUpdateService.cs into its own file under packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/SystemInfo/, keeping the Mohist.Server.SystemInfo namespace and every type/member name unchanged. Extract SystemUpdateJobState.cs (record + ActiveStatuses/TerminalStatuses), FileSystemSystemUpdateStore.cs (ISystemUpdateStore + impl, owning lock acquisition, atomic rename, SaveIfCurrentAsync), ProcessSystemUpdateCommandRunner.cs (ISystemUpdateCommandRunner + impl + SystemCommandRequest/SystemCommandResult), and HttpSystemReadinessProbe.cs (ISystemReadinessProbe + impl + SystemReadinessResult, owning health/root/bundled-asset HTML parsing). SystemUpdateService.cs keeps only update-job orchestration and retains SystemUpdateService.IsActive. Do not touch the sibling files (RuntimeBuildInfo, ServiceStatusChecker, GitSourceInspector, PhysicalFileSystem, SystemdInstallDetector, SystemdUnitParser, SystemInfoService).
acceptanceCriteria: FileSystemSystemUpdateStore and ISystemUpdateStore are declared in a file separate from SystemUpdateService, owning file-lock acquisition, atomic temp-file rename, and SaveIfCurrentAsync
ProcessSystemUpdateCommandRunner, ISystemUpdateCommandRunner, SystemCommandRequest, and SystemCommandResult are declared in a file separate from SystemUpdateService
HttpSystemReadinessProbe, ISystemReadinessProbe, and SystemReadinessResult are declared in a file separate from SystemUpdateService, owning health/root/bundled-asset HTML parsing
SystemUpdateJobState record with ActiveStatuses/TerminalStatuses is declared in a file separate from SystemUpdateService
Every extracted type keeps namespace Mohist.Server.SystemInfo and identical type/member names and record positional parameters

SystemUpdateService contains only orchestration (start, build→restart-server→wait-for-reconnect, CLI outcome recording, supersession, runtime-consistency reporting) and retains SystemUpdateService.IsActive

MohistServiceRegistration is unedited and still resolves ISystemUpdateStore→FileSystemSystemUpdateStore, ISystemUpdateCommandRunner→ProcessSystemUpdateCommandRunner, ISystemReadinessProbe→HttpSystemReadinessProbe with original lifetimes; SystemUpdateService remains a singleton
HTTP route/method/status-code and persisted JSON shapes are unchanged
Sibling files (RuntimeBuildInfo.cs, ServiceStatusChecker.cs, GitSourceInspector.cs, PhysicalFileSystem.cs, SystemdInstallDetector.cs, SystemdUnitParser.cs, SystemInfoService.cs) show no diff
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds with zero warnings (TreatWarningsAsErrors)
npm test (server) passes with existing SystemUpdateServiceSpecs unchanged — this is a behavior-preserving relocation
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/SystemInfo/{SystemUpdateJobState.cs,FileSystemSystemUpdateStore.cs,ProcessSystemUpdateCommandRunner.cs,HttpSystemReadinessProbe.cs,SystemUpdateService.cs} with SystemUpdateService.cs reduced to orchestration; all existing specs green
tasks.notes: Pure mechanical relocation — no logic change. Keep SystemUpdateService.IsActive on SystemUpdateService (the store references it at the former :119). Verify with a diff that only SystemInfo/ files changed.

tasks.title: Consolidate state-transition templates into shared helpers
tasks.description: Collapse the 13+ hand-rolled 'construct next state → append log → save → maybe release lock' sites and the duplicated failed-state constructions into shared helpers on SystemUpdateService. Add a PersistTransitionAsync helper owning append-log (bounded to 200 entries, most-recent retained) → set UpdatedAt → SaveAsync → optional ReleaseLockAsync (release strictly after save). Generalize the existing FailAsync so it is the single definition of the failed transition (covering reason, optional stage, optional outcome, optional UnavailableCapability, optional logStage/logMessage, releaseLock). Route every build/restart/waiting pipeline step, readiness-driven waiting/ready transition, supersession, recovered, and CLI-outcome recording through PersistTransitionAsync, and every catch block and non-zero-exit branch through FailAsync. Remove all inline duplicates.
acceptanceCriteria: A PersistTransitionAsync helper owns the shared tail: append log capped at 200 entries → stamp UpdatedAt → SaveAsync → optional ReleaseLockAsync, with ReleaseLockAsync running strictly after SaveAsync
FailAsync is generalized to cover every existing failed-state shape (StartAsync catch, RunUpdate catch, non-zero exit, restore failure) and is the single definition of the failed transition
Every transition site (pipeline steps, readiness waiting/ready, supersession, recovered, CLI-outcome) invokes PersistTransitionAsync instead of inline AppendLog + SaveAsync
Every catch block and non-zero-exit branch delegates to FailAsync instead of hand-writing `state with { Status = "failed", ... }`
A source audit finds no `state with { Status = "failed"` expression outside the shared failure handler
A source audit finds no inline `AppendLog(...) + await _store.SaveAsync(...)` sequence outside the shared helper
The 200-entry log cap is defined exactly once (inside the shared helper)
Persisted status values, stage labels, reason strings, log-entry stages/messages, CompletedAt/UpdatedAt timestamps, and lock-release points are identical to before consolidation for every transition
Recovered transition keeps its own shape but routes persist+release through PersistTransitionAsync
npm test (server) passes with existing SystemUpdateServiceSpecs unchanged
New unit/spec tests assert transition sites route through the shared helper and that the audit finds a single definition of each transition template
tasks.output: SystemUpdateService.cs with PersistTransitionAsync + generalized FailAsync and all inline duplicates removed; existing specs green plus new audit/purity tests
tasks.notes: Behavior-preserving relocation of duplicated logic. A single DateTimeOffset.UtcNow stamps both UpdatedAt and the log entry per transition (pre-existing wall-clock usage retained, not in scope to inject TimeProvider). Field deltas stay at call sites; only the shared tail moves into the helper.

tasks.title: Separate the status query from the job-advancement command (CQS fix)
tasks.description: Resolve the command/query violation in GetLatestStatusAsync by splitting it into a strictly read-only query and a new AdvanceActiveJobAsync command. The query reads only persisted state (plus, if strictly needed to populate a response field, a non-mutating read of the running hash) and performs no command dispatch, no SaveAsync/SaveIfCurrentAsync, no ReleaseLockAsync. AdvanceActiveJobAsync owns the three advancement branches currently hidden in the query: (1) supersede a stale waiting-for-reconnect job whose runtime hash advanced past its source HEAD; (2) persist the waiting-for-reconnect transition when readiness fails and stage/reason would change (preserving the dedup gate); (3) on readiness success + hash match: persist ready → restart the runner → mark succeeded → release lock, in that exact ordering. GetStatusEnvelopeAsync becomes command-then-query: invoke AdvanceActiveJobAsync then GetLatestStatusAsync then wrap. Migrate the 8 GetLatestStatusAsync_* specs to assert against the polling flow and/or AdvanceActiveJobAsync, and add new specs asserting the query issues zero command dispatches, zero saves, and zero lock releases.
acceptanceCriteria: GetLatestStatusAsync is strictly read-only: invoking it for a running or waiting-for-reconnect job dispatches zero commands via ISystemUpdateCommandRunner
GetLatestStatusAsync performs no ISystemUpdateStore.SaveAsync / SaveIfCurrentAsync and leaves the persisted state file unchanged
GetLatestStatusAsync performs no ReleaseLockAsync; a subsequent start attempt is still rejected because the lock remains held
A new AdvanceActiveJobAsync command method owns the supersede, waiting-persist, and ready→restart→succeeded→release branches
GetStatusEnvelopeAsync invokes AdvanceActiveJobAsync then GetLatestStatusAsync (command-then-query) before wrapping the response
Success-path ordering is preserved: persist ready → restart runner → mark succeeded → release lock
Supersession persists a Superseded log entry referencing both the running git hash and source HEAD, with RunningGitHash reflecting the advanced runtime hash
Ready transition persists a Ready log entry referencing the readiness root asset path with reason stating runtime matches source HEAD and readiness passed
Readiness-failure dedup is preserved: same stage/reason produces no new log entry and no persist
An empty/zero running hash never triggers supersession; the job stays waiting-for-reconnect
Repeated polling still observes waiting-for-reconnect → succeeded (lock released, next start accepted) and → superseded transitions
The 8 GetLatestStatusAsync_* specs are migrated to assert against GetStatusEnvelopeAsync and/or AdvanceActiveJobAsync (behavior honored at polling-endpoint level, not the now-pure method)
New specs assert the query path issues zero command dispatches, zero saves, and zero lock releases
npm test (server) passes with all migrated + new system-update specs green
tasks.output: SystemUpdateService.cs with pure GetLatestStatusAsync + new AdvanceActiveJobAsync + command-then-query GetStatusEnvelopeAsync; migrated and new specs in SystemUpdateServiceSpecs.cs all green
tasks.notes: The extracted advancement code must already route through the shared helpers from T-002 so extraction is a clean relocation. HTTP verb stays GET (POST advance endpoint was explicitly rejected as contract-breaking); the command is named and separable for a future mechanical verb split. No state-transition semantics change — only the entry path changes.
